method_scope_conclusions.title: Persistent Homology-induced Graph Ensembles for Time Series Regressions
method_scope_conclusions.publication_status: Preprint; exact-title SSRN posted-content DOI10.2139/ssrn.5521531; no conference/journal verified
method_scope_conclusions.takeaway: PH death-time thresholds produce distinct graph supports. Separate temporal/GCN weights per graph feed shared graph-attention fusion and output MLP. Only aggregate regression loss is printed in scope. No GNN-backbone sharing, scorer-only feedback or uniform classifier pool stated.

method_scope_conclusions.title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus
method_scope_conclusions.takeaway: Independently initialized models receive own supervised loss plus stopped current-mean prediction consistency on unlabeled TRAIN inputs. Summed member losses update simultaneously. GNN+ protocol uses10% labeled data, gamma1 selected onZINC. No shared feature backbone or scorer/QK-only recipients printed.
method_scope_conclusions.relation_to_GRAND_GraphMix: Graph consistency/shared-view targets are already established; this is a concrete graph-ensemble member-quality comparator, not discovery of graph consistency.
method_scope_conclusions.full_label_possible_adaptation: Separately frozen consistency on TRAIN graph inputs while keeping all TRAIN labels in own supervised loss; explicitly an adaptation, no additional held molecule inputs.
method_scope_conclusions.low_label_possible_task: Prospectively fixed labeled subset within officialTRAIN; remainingTRAINinputs unlabeled to all matched methods.
method_scope_conclusions.data_boundary: Never move officialVALID/TEST graph-inductive molecule inputs into unlabeledTRAIN. Transductive node-input permission does not transfer to graph-inductive datasets.

decision: Adopt two new bounded graph-ensemble method scopes. Molecular ensemble consensus is an attributed ICML2026 comparator with a different low-label task; GRAND/GraphMix consistency ancestry remains established. No official VALID/TEST molecular input is admitted into TRAIN. No new compute or source recipe is admitted from this search; the existing graph-relation study remains active and unopened.
